I tested the patched version and the root issue still appears to be unfixed. After a network flap affecting a subnet router:
- Headscale process still hang during shutdown
- subnet router still does not receive peer updates for nodes that connect after the flap

So the current patch doesnt seem to fully resolve the stale-session path. I'm continuing to look into it

Thank you!

It would be really great if we somehow could trap this condition in a test.

I added a focused reproducer for this in `hscontrol/poll_test.go` (Codex helped me here), and removed the earlier writeMap timeout commit for now, since it seems unrelated to the root issue here, though it may still be worth adding separately later.

The updated fix takes a different approach:
- when stale-send cleanup removes a timed-out connection from multiChannelNodeConn, **it now also closes that session's map-response channel**
- this makes the old serveLongPoll exit instead of lingering as an orphaned stale session
- the client can then reconnect normally and receive a fresh initial full map, which should let a subnet router learn about peers it missed while the old session was stale
- RemoveNode is also kept tolerant of the channel already having been removed earlier, since that is now an expected cleanup order

I'm still learning the Headscale codebase, so I may be missing some nuance here, but this seems closer to the actual failure mode than the previous approach. I've deployed the updated version in my installation and will monitor it.

The [last change](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale/pull/3130/changes/0c07f2ffc9234f59f7085d1b284348b5c7d05fc1) was needed because TestBatcherConcurrentClients/LockFree started failing with `send on closed channel`. What was happening:
- AddNode registers the connection and sends initialMap
- at the same time, another path can decide that session is stale and tear it down
- if the batcher closes the map-response channel from its side, that can race with the initialMap send and panic

I'm not completely happy about changing the AddNode interface for this, but I think it's the cleaner fix.

I first tried to fix it by holding a mutex while sending initialMap, but that didn't feel right. That send can block for a while, and keeping the per-node lock held during it means reconnects, cleanup, stale-session removal, and shutdown for that node can all get stuck behind one slow send.

So instead of trying to protect c <- initialMap with a long-held lock, the latest change makes session teardown explicit: the batcher stops the old session through its cancel path, and no longer closes the data channel underneath senders. That fixes the closed-channel panic in the churn test and feels like a better ownership model too (but makes the AddNode interface a bit wider).
Tailscale HEAD now appears to require Go 1.26.1, while this branch and main are still on 1.26.0. Should I bump Go to 1.26.1 in this PR?

> Should I bump Go to 1.26.1 in this PR?

You can bump it to unblock yourself, then we could rebase it away if we get it in before you.
Ok, I bumped Go to 1.26.1 here. I also verified that the previously failing Tailscale docker build now passes locally.

message:
mapper: handle RemoveNode after channel cleanup

A connection can already be removed from multiChannelNodeConn by the stale-send cleanup path before serveLongPoll reaches its deferred RemoveNode call. In that case RemoveNode used to return early on "channel not found" and never updated the node's connected state.

Drop that early return so RemoveNode still checks whether any active connections remain and marks the node disconnected when the last one is gone.

mapper: close stale map channels after send timeouts

When the batcher timed out sending to a node, it removed the channel from multiChannelNodeConn but left the old serveLongPoll goroutine running on that channel. That left a live stale session behind: it no longer received new updates, but it could still keep the stream open and block shutdown.

Close the pruned channel when stale-send cleanup removes it so the old map session exits after draining any buffered update.

poll: stop stale map sessions through an explicit teardown hook

When stale-send cleanup prunes a connection from the batcher, the old serveLongPoll session needs an explicit stop signal. Pass a stop hook into AddNode and trigger it when that connection is removed, so the session exits through its normal cancel path instead of relying on channel closure from the batcher side.
